title: Binary codimension-seven LCD distance-four exceptions
summary: Determine the exact optimum minimum distance at the 19 residual lengths for binary Euclidean LCD codes of codimension seven.

formal_statement.body: For each $n\in\{34,36,38,40,42,44,46,48,50,52,54,56,58,59,60,61,62,63,64\}$, decide whether a binary Euclidean LCD code with parameters $[n,n-7,4]$ exists. Equivalently, determine whether $d_2^E(n,n-7)=4$ or $d_2^E(n,n-7)=3$ at every listed length.

scope.domain: Binary Euclidean linear complementary dual codes of codimension seven
assumptions: The TIT source already bounds the optimum minimum distance to either 3 or 4 at every listed length
scope.unresolved_remainder: An accessible version-one preprint claims $d_2^E(n,n-7)=3$ for all 19 residual lengths, thereby ruling out every target code. Peer-reviewed publication or independent confirmation of that complete negative classification remains outstanding.

progress.summary: The TIT source reduces the codimension-seven problem to 19 lengths where the optimum minimum distance is either 3 or 4.
A public preprint proves a cap-based nonexistence theorem and claims that the optimum is 3 at every one of the 19 residual lengths.
